heading: Calling a method in another language
body:
`@Gateway` declares a method that another language answers. Write it like a request method: a method without a body in an `HTTPClient` contract. In JavaScript and TypeScript its answer is `Promise<BehaviorJsonValue | void>`. The annotation names one of two targets.

`{"class":"server/services/ReportService.java","method":"summarize"}` names a role file in another Yon language. `method` is optional. By default, it is the name of the annotated method. Tachyon builds a small unit in the language of the target. The unit puts together the role files of that language. It creates the class with its own dependencies. It calls only the methods that callers declared. The target runs like a route: it has the same environment and its own managed storage.

`{"command":["python3","server/helpers/forecast.py"]}` names a program. The first entry is a program on the `PATH` of the server. Every entry that contains a slash is a file under `server/helpers/`. No shell runs, and the arguments of the call never go on the command line. The program reads `{"method": "forecast", "arguments": [3]}` on stdin (standard input) and writes only the JSON result on stdout (standard output). Exit status 0 means success. Any other status is a failure. The program gets only the baseline environment (`PATH`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL` and `TMPDIR` on Unix; `PATH`, `PATHEXT`, `SYSTEMROOT`, `WINDIR`, `COMSPEC`, `TEMP` and `TMP` on Windows) and the names you add to the allowlist (`server.environment`, see Environment variables for handlers). It never gets `YON_APPLICATION_JSON` or the `YON_RESOURCE_*` values.

The positional arguments of the method travel as JSON. The return value of the other side becomes the result of the method. Typed languages use their JSON value type: `Object` in Java, `Any?` in Kotlin, `BehaviorJsonValue` in TypeScript, `BehaviorValue` in Go. These are the limits: at most 32 arguments; 1 MiB of JSON each way, at most 32 levels deep and 10,000 values; 64 calls and 4 calls at the same time per request; and the time left in the request. Each call starts a new process, so a JVM or .NET target spends its start-up time again on every call.

A failure reaches the caller as a `BehaviorError`. Its code is `invalid`, `timeout`, `capacity` or `adapter`, and its message is always `Gateway call failed.`. The messages of the target and its stderr (error output) never reach the caller. The server logs only a `handler.gateway_failed` event with the code. Only one hop (one call from one language to another) is allowed. Tachyon refuses a target class that declares its own gateway.

The build checks every target. It fails with `TY1312` when the file is missing or outside `server/`. It also fails when the file is in the caller's own language. In that case, inject it instead. It also fails when it is not a Yon language. It fails when the target has no concrete instance method of that name. It also fails when the method takes a different number of arguments. It fails when the method uses a type that is not the JSON value type of the language. Tachyon selects Java, Groovy, Kotlin and C# overloads by argument count and JSON types, not by source order. Overloads are methods with the same name but different parameters. Ambiguous signatures also fail with `TY1312`. So do callers that ask for different argument counts for the same target method. Rust target methods use `&self`. Tachyon refuses a method that consumes `self` or borrows `&mut self`. A Go target method is exported. So Tachyon calls the method whose name starts with an upper-case letter (`summarize` calls `Summarize`). A misused annotation fails with `TY1308`. This happens in Tac, on an HTTP verb method, or together with another method annotation. `server/gateways/` is reserved for the generated units (`TY1310`). A missing program fails at start-up with `TY2112`, and Firecracker isolation refuses gateways (`TY2010`).

Every Yon language below calls a class in another language. The examples also show an explicit Python command target. Lua has no tab here, because the build refuses Gateway in Lua Yon code with TY1308.

C++ has no tab here, because C++ Yon code has only route controllers so far: the build refuses `HTTPClient` in C++ with `TY1308` (ADR 0099).
